title: A post-TDD refresh can seal the Build binding again over ship's own inbox consumption
summary: In cycle 1830 the repair round ran TDD and Build with no change. The post-TDD refresh then sealed the Build handoff again at 8eb4ced1. That digest covers 14 paths: the 12 paths of the Build and the two paths of ship's inbox consumption. So the Build binding took in a change that ship made, not the Builder. The two-phase landing (ADR-0039 §8.1) unwinds the lane before Audit or Build sees ship's commit, so this path is now rare. It still occurs when the unwind declines, or when a lane holds a commit from an older binary.
fix: Make the refresh refuse a material change that is only inbox consumption pairs, or measure from the audited shape. A refresh must never take ship's consumption into the Build binding.
acceptance: A refresh over a lane that holds ship's consumption commit does not seal the consumption paths (red first)
A refresh over a real Build change still seals it (preservation)
routed_reason: out of scope for the ship-landing lane (brief: secondary finding); the fix is in core and explanationdocs, protected surfaces
